blocks.content: Indian Railways serves as the backbone of national transport, connecting diverse regions across the country.

rows: Main routes and heavy freight corridors

items: Memorize the headquarters of all 18 Railway Zones, especially newly added ones like South Coast Railway (Visakhapatnam).
Standard track gauge measurements (Broad Gauge = 1676 mm) are frequently asked in RRB NTPC and JE exams.
Key historical dates: First train (1853), First electric train (1925), and Nationalisation of Railways (1951).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The first passenger train ran on April 16, 1853, covering a distance of 34 km between Bombay (Bori Bunder) and Thane.
Indian Railways is divided into 18 administrative zones, with the South Coast Railway zone headquartered at Visakhapatnam being the newest.
The official mascot of Indian Railways is 'Bholu'—an elephant dressed as a railway guard holding a green lamp.
The Acworth Committee recommended the separation of the Railway Budget from the General Budget in 1924, which was merged back in 2017.
